answer: Coordination Escrow Pricing. Each identity posts an escrow whose size scales with how many simultaneous actions it takes against distinct counterparties; the price climbs steeply toward a zenith as one identity fans out. Fees are refunded only when actions land near the median rate of a peer cluster, so mass parallel coordination loses most of its escrow at the summit of activity. A sybil farm must therefore fund each fake identity separately to avoid the hollow returns of collapsed refunds, multiplying attacker cost per node.
